stories.title: $300M McKinney Music Venue to Open Early 2027
stories.excerpt: Venu Holdings has been working on the 20,000-seat amphitheater since last year, and expects it to be open for its first concert early next year. The Dallas Business Journal reports the parking garage is near completion, while the seating bowl and canopy are taking shape. The first show is expected to take place shortly after construction wraps up in the first quarter of 2027. Venu has not yet announced an opening act or a potential naming rights sponsor. The $300 million facility is being built through a public-private partnership between Venu, the City of McKinney, the McKinney Economic Development Corp. and the McKinney Community Development Corp. Venu has projects underway in Oklahoma, Houston and El Paso, with another facility planned in Chattanooga, Tennessee. The company, which operates venues in Colorado Springs, Colorado and Gainesville, Georgia, is also exploring an expansion into Northern Colorado. The post $300M McKinney Music Venue to Open Early 2027 appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Venu Holdings $300M amphitheater in McKinney, Texas opening Q1 2027.
20,000-seat venue via public-private partnership with City of McKinney.
Venu expanding regionally: projects in Oklahoma, Houston, El Paso, Chattanooga, Colorado.
stories.summary: Venu Holdings is constructing a $300 million, 20,000-seat amphitheater in McKinney, Texas through a public-private partnership with the city and local development corporations, with opening expected in early 2027. The parking garage is nearing completion while seating and canopy work continues. Venu is simultaneously developing venues in Oklahoma, Houston, El Paso, and Chattanooga, signaling aggressive regional expansion.
stories.impact: Entertainment venues anchor mixed-use and master-planned communities, driving foot traffic and property values in secondary markets. McKinney's amphitheater will generate incremental demand for nearby multifamily housing—particularly rental stock serving event staff, visiting performers, and leisure visitors—and validates the market's ability to support higher-density development. Monitor timing of major tenant announcements and naming sponsorship to gauge draw and confirm demand signals for adjacent multifamily sites.

stories.title: Trumark Acquires 195 Lots for Two New Bishop Ranch Neighborhoods
stories.excerpt: Trumark Homes is adding to the residential component of Sunset Development’s Bishop Ranch mixed-use megaproject in San Ramon, acquiring 195 lots for The Trails in Bishop Ranch. Located on the northwestern land of Bishop Ranch, the project’s two new neighborhoods include Promenade at The Trails, with 67 three-story single-family homes; and Paseo at The Trails, with 128 three-story townhomes. “The connectivity and tranquility that Bishop Ranch offers are appealing advantages for those working in the area, and we anticipate high demand from prospective homebuyers seeking those same qualities where they call home,” said Tony Bosowski, Northern California Division president at Trumark Homes. The Trails in Bishop Ranch is connected to the 600-acre master-planned community’s numerous and distinct elements, most notably City Center, its 300,000-square-foot, open-air shopping, dining and entertainment destination, according to Trumark. The launch of sales is planned for fall 2027. The post Trumark Acquires 195 Lots for Two New Bishop Ranch Neighborhoods appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Trumark Homes acquires 195 lots at Bishop Ranch, San Ramon, California.
Two neighborhoods: 67 three-story single-family homes, 128 three-story townhomes; sales launch fall 2027.
Bishop Ranch is 600-acre mixed-use with 300K SF retail/dining City Center.
stories.summary: Trumark Homes has acquired 195 lots within Sunset Development's Bishop Ranch mixed-use megaproject in San Ramon, California, adding two residential neighborhoods: Promenade at The Trails (67 single-family homes) and Paseo at The Trails (128 townhomes). Sales are slated to launch in fall 2027. The neighborhoods will benefit from integration with Bishop Ranch's 300,000-square-foot City Center and broader connectivity.
stories.impact: This is a for-sale product play, not rental multifamily, but signals strong absorption momentum and developer confidence in San Ramon's East Bay submarket. The staggered delivery and anchor tenancy around City Center suggest sustained demand for residential in the East Bay's employment corridor. For multifamily developers, this validates the trade area and highlights the competitive positioning of master-planned communities—consider rental vs. ownership-product mix and pricing when evaluating competing sites in the 680 corridor.

stories.title: Camelback Offices Trades for $86M
stories.excerpt: Esplanade III, a 222,820-square-foot trophy office building on 2415 E. Camelback Road, sold for $86 million. The 10-story building was acquired by Southwest Value Partners, a joint venture made up of Transwestern and C-III Capital Partners. JLL brokers Ben Geelan, Will Mast and Charlie von Arentschildt represented the seller. The Phoenix Business Journal reports the Transwestern partnership acquired the office building in July 2019 for $60.2 million in an all-cash deal, according to Maricopa County records. The building is currently 83.4% leased with a weighted average unexpired lease term of 4.4 years. Vestar, Vanguard Realty Advisors, Barclay Group, Velocity Retail Group, Husch Blackwell, Pederson Group, Inc. and Velocity Retail Group are among the tenants at Esplanade III. The post Camelback Offices Trades for $86M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Esplanade III, Phoenix office (222,820 SF) sells for $86M; acquired for $60.2M in July 2019.
Building 83.4% leased, 4.4-year weighted average lease term; owned by Transwestern/C-III Capital.
43% appreciation over ~7 years reflects office asset recovery but compressed lease renewals ahead.
stories.summary: Esplanade III, a 222,820-square-foot, 10-story trophy office building at 2415 E. Camelback Road in Phoenix, sold for $86 million to a Transwestern and C-III Capital Partners joint venture. The building was previously acquired for $60.2 million in July 2019. Current occupancy stands at 83.4% with a weighted average unexpired lease term of 4.4 years.
stories.impact: Office asset appreciation and refinancing in Phoenix do not directly affect multifamily demand, but the 4.4-year WALT signals near-term lease expirations and renewal risk in a market where office fundamentals remain soft. Multifamily developers should track Camelback corridor office tenant leasing activity and any major relocations; office consolidation or flight could dampen local employment and slow multifamily rent growth expectations in east Phoenix submarkets.

stories.title: Nonprofit Biohub, Software Firm Fundraise Up Lease 20K SF at 100-104 Fifth Avenue
stories.excerpt: Two nonprofit-related tenants are moving to an office just west of Manhattan’s Union Square. In the largest deal, the Chan Zuckerberg Biohub, better known simply as Biohub, secured a 10,666-square-foot lease at Sovereign Partners’ 100-104 Fifth Avenue, Commercial Observer has learned. The nonprofit biomedical research organization will occupy the entire ninth floor of the 20-story tower at the southwest corner of Fifth Avenue and West 15th Street, according to sources. The building is one block west of Union Square. Biohub was founded in 2016 by Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan, with the goal to cure, prevent and manage human diseases. The company currently lists offices and a research laboratory at Columbia University’s Studebaker Building at 615 West 131st Street. Sources said the move marks a relocation from a Biohub office near Union Square, but no address in the neighborhood was found. Biohub was represented by Newmark’s David Falk, Mike Courson and Dylan Weisman. Falk also represented Sovereign Partners alongside Daniel Levine and Paige Raisides. A spokesperson for Newmark did not respond to a request for comment on the transaction. The nonprofit will be in good company at the Fifth Avenue office tower. Fundraise Up, a fundraising platform designed for nonprofit organizations, has signed its own lease at the building. Fundraise Up took 9,522 square feet across the entire seventh floor, in a relocation from 219 36th Street in Brooklyn’s Industry City complex. The lease terms for both of the recent deals were not disclosed, but asking rents in the building range from $110 to $150 per square foot, according to the source. Cushman & Wakefield’s David Hoffman, Sam Hoffman and Louden Sheehan negotiated the lease on behalf of Fundraise Up. The same Newmark team represented the landlord. bullets: Chan Zuckerberg Biohub leases 10,666 SF (entire 9th floor) at 100-104 Fifth Avenue, Manhattan.
Nonprofit biomedical research organization relocating within Union Square area.
Biohub maintains separate research lab at Columbia University's Studebaker Building, Upper Manhattan.
stories.summary: The Chan Zuckerberg Biohub, a nonprofit biomedical research organization founded by Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan in 2016, has leased the entire ninth floor (10,666 square feet) of Sovereign Partners' 100-104 Fifth Avenue, one block west of Union Square in Manhattan. The lease marks a relocation from a nearby Union Square office. Biohub also operates a research laboratory at Columbia University.
stories.impact: Minor relevance to multifamily development. Biohub's leasing reflects office market strength around Union Square but does not signal new employment density or population inflows that would drive housing demand. Monitor if biotech talent concentration near Union Square or Upper Manhattan research facilities generates secondary housing demand among researchers and support staff—but this single lease is insufficient to establish a demand signal.

stories.title: Queens’ Apartment Pipeline Shallowest in a Decade — But New Supply On the Way
stories.excerpt: The world’s borough might attract some new residents soon. There’s a multifamily squeeze in Queens as the rental market tightens amid a dip in new construction, according to new data from CoStar. But experts on the borough’s housing market say this drop won’t last too much longer. The vacancy rate in Queens’ multifamily market declined to 2.08 percent in the second quarter of 2026, versus 2.39 percent for the same quarter in 2025. Meanwhile, stabilized vacancy hit a record low of 1.3 percent, which CoStar called “well below the metro average,” and the apartment pipeline has declined 76 percent since early 2024, falling from 10,881 units under construction to just 2,597 during the second quarter of 2026. That represents the borough’s shallowest pipeline in at least a decade, according to the CoStar analysis. “I think it’s that classic story of supply and demand,” said Victor Rodriguez, senior director of market analytics at CoStar. “We saw vacancies drift upward in recent years in Queens, just because there’s so much being built. It does take time for those newer buildings to lease up, especially as you are looking to add thousands upon thousands of units every single year. But, when the supply story changes, the demand story doesn’t necessarily change, and what we have here, especially throughout Queens, is a major decline in that construction pipeline.” The construction pipeline slowed recently due to the passage of the city’s 485-x initiative — a tax abatement program designed to incentivize more affordable housing that comes with heftier construction wage costs for projects over 100 units — and due to some developers waiting for the passage of the housing-friendly One LIC rezoning in Long Island City, according to Eric Benaim, co-founder and CEO of real estate group Modern Spaces. “There were a lot of projects that were on pause because they were waiting for 485-x to happen,” Benaim said. “That threw a wrench into a lot of projects, especially b
bullets: Queens multifamily pipeline declined 76% since early 2024: 10,881 to 2,597 units under construction.
Q2 2026 vacancy 2.08% (down from 2.39% YoY); stabilized vacancy hit record-low 1.3%.
Shallowest pipeline in decade; new supply expected soon per CoStar analysis.
stories.summary: Queens' multifamily rental market is experiencing a sharp supply squeeze. The apartment pipeline has plummeted 76 percent since early 2024, from 10,881 units to just 2,597 units under construction as of Q2 2026—the borough's shallowest pipeline in at least a decade. Vacancy rates have compressed correspondingly: overall vacancy fell to 2.08 percent year-over-year, while stabilized vacancy hit a record low of 1.3 percent, well below the metro average. Market analysts expect new supply to arrive imminently.
stories.impact: CRITICAL for multifamily developers. Queens' supply drought and sub-2% vacancies signal acute undersupply and strong rent-growth tailwinds—a rare window to acquire underbid land, expedite entitlements, and lock in construction at current pricing before competing projects deliver. The 76% pipeline collapse suggests either financing constraints, zoning barriers, or prior overbuilding that has now absorbed; investigate which. Developers with shovel-ready projects in Queens (Forest Hills, Long Island City, Astoria, Jamaica) should accelerate; rents will compress quickly once the pinched pipeline absorbs demand. This is a high-priority market signal.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Closes Self-Storage Portfolio Sale in Oregon
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap completed the sale of a six-property, 537,962-square-foot, 3,545-unit Secure Storage self-storage portfolio in Ashland, Bend, Prineville, Redmond, Hood River, and Hillsboro, Oregon. “This family-owned and operated portfolio reflects true pride of ownership as each of the six properties has been meticulously maintained and consistently reinvested in throughout the duration of ownership,” said Adam Schlosser, executive managing director of the LeClaire-Schlosser Group of Marcus & Millichap. “That quality, combined with strong in-place performance across every asset, gave the next investor a rare opportunity to acquire a turnkey portfolio with room to grow.” Schlosser, Keith Phillips, and Dean Trammell of Marcus & Millichap, in association with David Tabata, Marcus & Millichap’s Oregon broker of record, represented the seller. Ground-level access spans 100% of the portfolio’s rentable square footage, and two of the six properties include dedicated land for future expansion. The post Marcus & Millichap Closes Self-Storage Portfolio Sale in Oregon appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap sells 6-property self-storage portfolio, Oregon (537,962 SF, 3,545 units).
Properties in Ashland, Bend, Prineville, Redmond, Hood River, Hillsboro; turnkey, ground-level access.
Two assets include land for expansion; family-owned, fully maintained.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of a six-property, 537,962-square-foot self-storage portfolio operated under the Secure Storage brand across Ashland, Bend, Prineville, Redmond, Hood River, and Hillsboro, Oregon. The 3,545-unit portfolio features 100 percent ground-level access and two properties with dedicated expansion land. The properties are described as well-maintained, turnkey assets with strong in-place performance.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Self-storage is a separate asset class with different capital sources, underwriting, and operational profiles. No signal on Oregon multifamily supply, demand, or labor market dynamics.

stories.title: Citadel Care Centers Lands $51M to Build Nursing Facility Near Aventura
stories.excerpt: Citadel Care Centers broke ground on a skilled nursing facility in North Miami Beach, Fla., after securing a $50.9 million loan, property records show. The financing from PNC Bank covers a 3.2-acre site, occupying a full block at 1875 and 1800 Northeast 167th Street, adjacent to Northeast 19th Avenue, about three miles south of Aventura. The new development will rise four stories and include a parking garage. It’s unclear whether the existing 50,088-square-foot Aventura Plaza Rehabilitation & Nursing Center, which occupies about half the parcel, will remain. A representative for New York-based Citadel Care Centers could not be reached for comment. The financing comes as Florida’s senior population is expected to grow about 4 percent annually through 2030, according to Colliers. Occupancy in senior housing properties has stabilized to just over 90 percent in the first quarter of 2026, up from roughly 80 percent five years ago. Sales of assisted living facilities have ticked up in recent months. Earlier this month, PGIM Real Estate sold a 7-acre property in Delray Beach for at least $140 million, marking one of the priciest South Florida retirement home sales in recent years. Healthpeak Properties bought a 136-unit facility in Boynton Beach for at least $62 million, also this month. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Citadel Care Centers secures $50.9M PNC Bank loan for skilled nursing facility, North Miami Beach.
3.2-acre site at 1875/1800 Northeast 167th Street, ~3 miles south of Aventura; 4-story building.
Florida senior population forecast to grow 4% annually through 2030; senior occupancy at 90%+ Q1 2026.
stories.summary: Citadel Care Centers has secured $50.9 million in financing from PNC Bank to construct a skilled nursing facility on a 3.2-acre parcel in North Miami Beach, Florida, about three miles south of Aventura. The four-story development will occupy a full block at 1875 and 1800 Northeast 167th Street and include a parking garage. The financing comes as Florida's senior population is projected to grow approximately 4 percent annually through 2030, and senior housing occupancy has stabilized above 90 percent as of Q1 2026.
stories.impact: Senior housing development signals aging-in-place demand in South Florida but does not directly drive multifamily rental demand. However, the 4% annual senior population growth through 2030 in Florida creates secondary demand for independent and assisted-living rental housing (age-restricted or wellness-focused multifamily). Developers should model senior-skewing demographics in Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach submarkets and consider mixed-income, age-restricted or active-adult-friendly rental products. Monitor capital availability for senior-focused multifamily paralleling this skilled-nursing facility push.

stories.title: Southern Land Co. Inks $165.9M Construction Loan for Upper Kirby Mixed-Use Project
stories.excerpt: Southern Land Co. has secured $165.9 million in financing for a mixed-use development underway in Houston’s Upper Kirby area. The Houston Business Journal reports that Bank OZK issued the loan to support the construction of the 2811 Kirby development. The project broke ground in April. The 2-acre, 953,000-square-foot development at 2811 Kirby Drive, near the intersection of Kirby Drive and Kipling Street, will include two towers — one for offices and one for apartments — and approximately 15,000 square feet of ground-level restaurant space. The 38-story Lily River Oaks luxury multifamily building will have 331 apartments, including 18 penthouses. A separate 10-story commercial tower will offer Class AA office space totaling approximately 107,000 square feet. Stream Realty Partners is leading leasing efforts for the office component. Southern Land Co. expects to deliver the project in 2028. The development team includes Andres Construction as general contractor and Solomon Cordwell Buenz as architect and interior designer. The post Southern Land Co. Inks $165.9M Construction Loan for Upper Kirby Mixed-Use Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Southern Land Co. secures $165.9M construction loan from Bank OZK for Upper Kirby mixed-use, Houston.
2811 Kirby: 953K SF, 2-acre project with 38-story luxury multifamily (331 apts, 18 penthouses) + 10-story office (107K SF).
Project broke ground April 2026; Lily River Oaks is the residential tower.
stories.summary: Southern Land Co. has obtained $165.9 million in construction financing from Bank OZK for the 2811 Kirby development, a 953,000-square-foot, 2-acre mixed-use project in Houston's Upper Kirby area that broke ground in April 2026. The development includes two towers: the 38-story Lily River Oaks luxury multifamily building with 331 apartments (including 18 penthouses) and a 10-story Class AA office tower with approximately 107,000 square feet. Ground-level space will feature approximately 15,000 square feet of restaurant space.
stories.impact: Strong capital availability for large-scale mixed-use development in Houston's Upper Kirby submarket signals sustained investor and lender confidence in urban-core, walkable residential in a high-barrier-to-entry corridor. The $165.9M loan validates market and financing appetite for luxury multifamily integrated with office and retail; this confirms rental demand and pricing power in the Kirby/Kipling corridor. For competing developers, monitor Lily River Oaks pre-leasing velocity and rent achievement to calibrate underwriting; mixed-use trophy projects typically command premium positioning and may compress NOI comparables for nearby Class B/C multifamily.

stories.title: BHI Lends $50M on SoCal Inland Empire Master-Planned Project
stories.excerpt: DO Capital Group has sealed $50 million of construction financing to develop a mixed-use master-planned community in Jurupa Valley, Calif., Commercial Observer has learned. BHI supplied the loan for the developer’s 239.2-acre The District at Jurupa Valley project in Southern California’s Inland Empire that will feature residential, retail, hospitality and logistics elements, as well as a business park and public parkland. Developers broke ground on the project June 4. “We specialize in structuring financing for complex, large-scale commercial real estate projects, and The District at Jurupa Valley exemplifies the kind of project we’re equipped to support,” Brian Jurczak, first vice president, commercial real estate lending at BHI, said in a statement. Located 50 miles east of Downtown Los Angeles, The District at Jurupa Valley development will consist of nearly 1,200 housing units, a shopping center with restaurants, and a 122-room Woodspring Suites hotel, The Press Enterprise previously reported. Bridge Logistics Properties also acquired more than 68 acres of the site for an industrial facility. Matthew Dugally, co-founding principal at DO Capital Group, said in a statement that the loan from BHI “has helped lay the foundation for a destination that will create new opportunities for residents, businesses, and the broader Jurupa Valley community for years to come.” Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BHI lends $50M to DO Capital for The District at Jurupa Valley, California (239.2 acres).
Mixed-use master-planned: ~1,200 housing units, retail, 122-room hotel, logistics, business park, parkland.
Inland Empire, 50 miles east of Downtown LA; broke ground June 2026.
stories.summary: BHI has provided $50 million in construction financing to DO Capital for The District at Jurupa Valley, a 239.2-acre mixed-use master-planned community in Jurupa Valley, California, located 50 miles east of Downtown Los Angeles in the Inland Empire. The project, which broke ground on June 4, will feature nearly 1,200 housing units, a shopping center with restaurants, a 122-room Woodspring Suites hotel, logistics facilities, a business park, and public parkland.
stories.impact: The District at Jurupa Valley signals ongoing investor appetite for large-scale master-planned communities in the Inland Empire with mixed-use residential, hospitality, and logistics components. The $50M construction facility and 1,200-unit pipeline confirm that Inland Empire supply is accelerating post-pandemic; monitor the pace of housing unit delivery and absorption. For multifamily developers, this validates Jurupa Valley as an emerging secondary market with logistics and e-commerce job drivers, but also signals competitive density—ensure your underwriting reflects delivered-supply velocity and rental rate assumptions in context of rising I.E. competition. Financing availability remains robust for large sponsors.

stories.title: Aarthi Bansidhar Joins Midwood as Chief Financial Officer
stories.excerpt: New York City-based private real estate firm Midwood Investment & Development has hired a new chief financial officer. Aarthi Bansidhar, a former managing director at Madison Capital, joined Midwood in June to lead its financial strategy, capital planning and performance management efforts across its national portfolio of office, residential and retail assets. “Aarthi brings an impressive track record of financial expertise and strategic leadership to the team, which will be invaluable as our company continues to grow and build out our national portfolio,” John Usdan, CEO of Midwood, said in a statement. Bansidhar has worked in finance and real estate for two decades, working at Madison for over 13 years. Before that, she worked as a senior manager of the asset management practice at Ernst & Young for close to nine years, according to her LinkedIn profile. “I’m eager to help strengthen our financial strategy and contribute to the company’s continued growth,” Bansidhar said in a statement. Bansidhar studied business management and accounting at Baruch College. Projects currently under development for Midwood include a 25-unit condominium project at 150 East 78th Street on Manhattan’s Upper East Side in collaboration with Robert A.M. Stern Architects, and a 31-story multifamily rental building at 210 South 12th Street in Philadelphia. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Aarthi Bansidhar joins Midwood as Chief Financial Officer in June 2026.
Former Madison Capital managing director; 20 years finance/real estate experience; led EY asset management.
Midwood builds office, residential, retail nationally; Bansidhar leads capital planning and portfolio performance.
stories.summary: Aarthi Bansidhar has joined New York City–based Midwood Investment & Development as Chief Financial Officer, effective June 2026. Bansidhar was previously a managing director at Madison Capital and spent nearly nine years as a senior manager of Ernst & Young's asset management practice. Over her 20-year career in finance and real estate, she will lead Midwood's financial strategy, capital planning, and performance management across its national portfolio of office, residential, and retail assets.
stories.impact: No direct market impact. Executive hiring at a major national developer signals organizational confidence and growth planning but does not reveal market signals, supply trends, or capital constraints. Irrelevant to demand, supply, capital availability, or cost analysis for multifamily development.
